speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic. I understand you've had an episode of loss of consciousness; to help me determine the cause, can you tell me exactly what you were doing right before you passed out and whether you experienced any shaking or jerking movements?

speaker: Patient
text: 53-year-old male. The patient was brought to the emergency department after an episode of loss of consciousness that occurred 1 hour ago, immediately after micturating. His wife found him unconscious on the bathroom floor. He regained consciousness after about 30 seconds without any confusion or amnesia for the event. No history of urinary incontinence during the event.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Commotio Cordis / Vasovagal Syncope due to micturition (Micturition Syncope). The history of passing out immediately after urination with rapid recovery and no incontinence is classic for micturition syncope, where bladder emptying leads to a drop in venous return and hypotension. Commotio Cordis is a differential if he was struck by a projectile during the event, but the description suggests a spontaneous event upon finishing voiding. Given the classic presentation and lack of shaking, I am confident in this diagnosis without further testing at this moment.
